The only open-access measurement found of gas flow through as-printed FDM walls, and the basis for this project's position that the printed strut is structure, not the vacuum barrier. Caveats that ride on every number taken from it: the test articles are PLA printed through a 0.30 mm nozzle (not CF-nylon through 0.6 mm); the sealing test is a bubble/volumetric test at about 0.5 bar overpressure, sensitive to roughly mL/s flows - 9-10 orders of magnitude coarser than a vacuum leak budget in the 1e-5 mbar.L/s class, so 'completely blocked' in this paper does not mean vacuum-tight; the k = 0.98 threshold and the wall-thickness series (~0.5 mm perimeter-only walls often untenable at any k; >= 1.1 mm walls seal via a homogeneous inner layer) are from one lab, one printer, one slicer. Caveats that ride on every number taken from it: the test articles are PLA printed through a 0.30 mm nozzle (not CF-nylon through 0.6 mm); the sealing test is a bubble/volumetric test at about 0.5 bar overpressure, sensitive to roughly mL/s flows - 9-10 orders of magnitude coarser than a vacuum leak budget in the 1e-5 mbar.L/s class, so 'completely blocked' in this paper does not mean vacuum-tight; the k = 0.98 threshold and the wall-thickness series (~0.5 mm perimeter-only walls often untenable at any k; >= 1.1 mm walls seal via a homogeneous inner layer) are from one lab, one printer, one slicer. One chapter of a larger annual publication; the DOI 10.3133/mcs2022 identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2022, and [link] serves the helium chapter as this standalone PDF. The 2021 figures are marked estimated ('e') in the chapter itself, and the chapter's own footnote warns that Census Bureau export data for 2018-2021 'may be incorrect', with apparent consumption estimated at 40 Mm3/yr as a result. This is the baseline of the price series this project cites: $7.57/m3 is HE_PRICE_2021_USD_M3 in research/analysis/[link], the denominator of the +85%-in-two-years repricing. Note the wording: 'with some producers posting surcharges to this price' - the base price understates what buyers paid. One chapter of a larger annual publication; DOI 10.3133/mcs2024 identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024. The divisor is the φ in σ = 3p/φ, so it counts the octet lattice's own strut-lengths per Kelvin-cell volume: the lattice is FCC at half-pitch, so it runs three struts per cubic half-pitch, and a cell of span four half-pitches encloses 32 of those — 3 × 32 = 96, exactly. (Clip the infinite lattice against the cell and the measure is 102 strut-lengths, of which the 6 lying in the six square faces belong equally to the cell above: 96 again.) Putting 144 there would dilute the octet's stress with members that are not in the octet, and this article's numbers would stop agreeing with the array's — the one thing the demonstrator exists to prove.

Putting 144 there would dilute the octet's stress with members that are not in the octet, and this article's numbers would stop agreeing with the array's — the one thing the demonstrator exists to prove.

Rods only win where buckling stops governing — below about six diameters of length — and every member here is thirty to sixty diameters long. (The one place rods do belong is the floater's level-2 boom chords at ~1.7 mm, where no tube can be made.) Round beats a hexagonal section by 9.4% on Euler at identical mass, and by far more on the flight article, where the wall is thin enough that local buckling co-governs and a flat face has no curvature to stabilise it; hex would buy anti-rotation and a flat bonding land, and we need neither.

Caveats that ride on every number taken from it: the test articles are PLA printed through a 0.30 mm nozzle (not CF-nylon through 0.6 mm); the sealing test is a bubble/volumetric test at about 0.5 bar overpressure, sensitive to roughly mL/s flows - 9-10 orders of magnitude coarser than a vacuum leak budget in the 1e-5 mbar.L/s class, so 'completely blocked' in this paper does not mean vacuum-tight; the k = 0.98 threshold and the wall-thickness series (~0.5 mm perimeter-only walls often untenable at any k; >= 1.1 mm walls seal via a homogeneous inner layer) are from one lab, one printer, one slicer.
